# The system's input-source indicator (Caps Lock, 中/A) sits where it last
# heard the cursor is. It asks when a pane takes the keyboard and not again
# by itself: it stayed where a new pane's cursor was mid-way through the
# split's animation, before the shell's prompt (0.6.5's screens show it
# well to the right of the cursor). The pane tells it once the cursor or
# the pane has moved. (Off screen, this sees the pane tell it; that the
# indicator then follows is for the real screen.)
wait:1.0
caret-ask:go
expect-caret-told:go
# Output moves the cursor.
type:echo CARET
key:enter
wait:0.5
expect-caret-told:go
# A split, animated as in the app: the new pane takes the keyboard while it
# still slides in, and its prompt comes after.
motion:on
key:cmd+d
caret-ask:go
wait:1.2
expect-panes:2
expect-focus:2
expect-caret-told:go
# Back in the first pane, narrower now.
key:cmd+alt+left
caret-ask:go
wait:0.4
expect-focus:1
expect-caret-told:go
# The split closes: the pane left takes the room, animated.
key:cmd+alt+right
wait:0.4
key:cmd+w
wait:1.2
expect-panes:1
expect-caret-told:go
# The window dragged: nothing to draw, and the cursor is elsewhere on the screen.
move:40,-30
expect-caret-told:go
